content:
Remaining issues:

1. The statement is in Azerbaijani. Please provide the English statement, format N as [[N]], EVEN/ODD as {{constants}}, and line labels in <<bold>>. The stub also needs a write command. These points were already raised by Naglfae.

2. All four validators exactly repeat the corresponding public inputs: 10, 7, 0 and -5. Consequently, printing ODD only for 7 and -5, and EVEN for everything else passes the entire registered suite while being wrong for many valid inputs. Replace non-singleton cases with varied inputs of the same parity/sign and add negative-even and larger-magnitude coverage. The zero boundary can legitimately remain identical.

3. The complete output has only two possible values, which makes partial-score guessing unusually easy. This concern was already raised by selenae and Naglfae. Consider a task with a naturally more varied result.

The originality concern was already raised by selenae. A related accepted neighbor is Even or Odd Count:
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/150957b92daaee8868b38324d6357a571feac2
It uses the same parity classification but counts a list instead of classifying one integer. I found a close neighbor, not evidence of an exact duplicate or of who originated the idea.

Surely this already exists.
And puzzles with only two possible outputs are discouraged.

Description:
- The description must be in English, 'EVEN' and 'ODD' should be formatted as {{constants}}

Input/Output:
- The part that defines the input/output on each line ('Line 1:', 'Line 2:') should be set to <<bold>>,  'N' should be formatted as a [[variable]]

Constraints:
- 'N' should be formatted as a [[variable]]

Stub generator:
- Should include a 'write' statement

Note: 
- This clash has binary output as well
